name: Coral Gables
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Coral Gables, FL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Coral Gables, FL: tree lighting, Junior Orange Bowl Parade, Santa visits, NightGarden and more, all checked on host sites.
lede: Coral Gables celebrates Christmas with city-run events at Merrick Park and Holiday Park, a downtown parade, Santa visits and holiday shows. The City Beautiful also has gardens, historic houses and a free trolley to help families get around.
celebrates: The City of Coral Gables lights its Holiday Tree at Merrick Park in front of City Hall, then turns the lawn into Holiday Park. The city also sends Santa around town on a fire truck to hand out candy canes, and Merrick House, the founder's coral rock family home, hosts an open house with carols and crafts. Downtown, the Junior Orange Bowl's Miracle on the Mile Parade brings Santa to the streets, and carolers sing along the shopping blocks. Nearby, Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden and Actors' Playhouse on Miracle Mile add Santa days, a musical and evening garden lights.
lastyear: In 2025 the Junior Orange Bowl Parade was planned for Sunday, December 14, at 5 pm in downtown Coral Gables. The city's calendar called it the Miracle on the Mile Parade and said people of all ages were invited to enjoy the sights and sounds. The Junior Orange Bowl described that parade as 77 years of Coral Gables parade tradition. The same city calendar also listed the annual Christmas Tree Lighting and Hot Chocolate with Santa among its holiday events.
facts: Coral Gables was incorporated on April 29, 1925. George Merrick's family named their coral rock home Coral Gables, and the city later took the name. The Venetian Pool, which opened in 1924, was built in a former quarry that supplied the coral rock for early houses, and it is on the National Register of Historic Places. By October 1926 the young city had more than 4,000 structures. The Miami Biltmore Hotel opened on January 15, 1926, and the Junior Orange Bowl calls its parade the founding event of its youth festival.
trains: The city's free Coral Gables Trolley starts at the Douglas Road Metrorail Station, at 3060 SW 37 Court, and runs along Ponce de Leon Boulevard to Flagler Street. The University Metrorail station sits in Coral Gables near the University of Miami. Miami-Dade Transit also lists a downtown Metrorail stop with connections to Brightline and Tri-Rail. For real trains, the Gold Coast Railroad Museum is at 12450 SW 152nd Street in Miami, with rail cars to explore and a small Link train to ride.
train_links: Train rides, rail cars and a model train building at 12450 SW 152nd Street in Miami.
traditions: Christmas Tree Lighting at Merrick Park
The city lights its Holiday Tree beside City Hall with a stage show, carnival games, craft vendors and a visit from Santa.
After the lighting, the Merrick Park lawn becomes Holiday Park, where the city also runs Hot Chocolate with Santa.
Coral Gables firefighters drive Santa through the neighborhoods so children can wave and get candy canes.
The Junior Orange Bowl brings its holiday parade to downtown Coral Gables, ending with Santa's arrival.
The founder's coral rock home opens for carols, crafts, cookies and a toy drive for the fire department.
The city calendar lists carolers returning to downtown Coral Gables in December.
kidfact: The Merrick family named their home Coral Gables because it was built from coral rock, and the whole city later took the name.
faq: Where is the Coral Gables Christmas tree?

The city lights its Holiday Tree at Merrick Park in front of City Hall, 405 Biltmore Way. After the ceremony the lawn becomes Holiday Park, which stays open for the season with rides and photo backdrops. The city's events calendar lists the lighting as a free event, with an optional ticket for early access to the seating area.
Who runs the Coral Gables holiday parade?

The Junior Orange Bowl runs the Miracle on the Mile Parade through downtown Coral Gables. The organization calls it the founding event of its International Youth Festival and says Santa arrives at the end of the parade. The City of Coral Gables also lists the parade on its holiday events calendar.
Is there a free way to get around Coral Gables?

Yes. The Coral Gables Trolley is free and runs along Ponce de Leon Boulevard from the Douglas Road Metrorail Station to Flagler Street. A second route, Grand Avenue, runs from the same station through the historic McFarlane Homestead District. The city lists weekday and Saturday hours on its trolley page.
What can kids see at Merrick House?

Merrick House is the coral rock family home of George Merrick, the founder of Coral Gables. The city says visitors can view 14 rooms on a docent-guided tour and stroll 1.3 acres of grounds with a grotto, a Heritage Garden and a lily pond. The house is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Where can we get a Santa photo in Coral Gables?

Options include Photos with Santa at Coral Gables City Hall, Hot Chocolate with Santa at Holiday Park, Wednesdays with Santa at The Shops at Merrick Park, and Santa days at Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden. Each host sets its own rules, so check that event page for reservations, prices and resident only tickets.
